title: Signal Desktop conversations
whyItMatters: Signal keeps a local copy of every conversation, attachment and draft. The database is encrypted, but the folder shows the account existed and how much was kept.
source: Signal Desktop is an Electron app and keeps its profile in the XDG config directory; the source and docs name the Signal folder: https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop
notes: sql/db.sqlite is SQLCipher-encrypted and its key sits in the desktop keyring; attachments, drafts and logs sit beside it. Signed out does not mean deleted. The Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/org.signal.Signal/config/Signal.

cleanup.exportFirst: Save any photos or files you want to keep from the conversations: Signal keeps no copy of them on a server.
cleanup.signOut: On your phone, open Signal > Settings > Linked devices and unlink this computer, so the account no longer trusts it.
steps: In Signal Desktop, open Settings and choose Delete Data to clear the local message store.
Quit Signal Desktop from its tray icon.
Uninstall Signal from the App Center if you are removing the app itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes the local copy of every conversation, attachment and draft on this computer. The messages stay on the linked phone only.
